newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin considers union agreement with Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin considers union agreement with Belarus.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin was on Monday reviewing a draft agreement on forging closer ties with Belarus, the Kremlin said.

The presidential press service said the draft agreement, due to be signed in Moscow on Wednesday with Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko, was one of several documents Yeltsin was working on but gave no details.

The terms of the agreement have not been widely circulated and liberal leaders say Yeltsin is pushing ahead with integration with the neighbouring former Soviet republic too fast and without consulting the Russian people properly.

Kremlin sources said liberals in the government had mounted a rearguard action to prevent Yeltsin signing the document, which they fear could allow the hardline Lukashenko to gain a slice of power in Russia.
Russian liberals are also concerned by the economic implications of integration with the smaller and less wealthy state of about 10 million people where economic reforms have made less headway.
They question Lukashenko's commitment to human rights and freedom of speech following the expulsion of a correspondent working for a Russian television channel.
Lukashenko and Yeltsin agreed on April 2 last year to form a "community" between their two Slav states but few concrete steps have been taken towards this community so far.
